page: Microsoft Azure F4-2amds_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Famdsv7 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, with 2 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a 472 GB disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression benchmarks all rank in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-threaded performance is more limited, with stress-ng multi-core performance and PassMark CPU scores falling into the average category, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak (bottom 25%). Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both read and write operations are average, and static web serving throughput is weak at 5.52 GB/sec. For language model workloads, prompt processing for a medium 7B model is poor, though text generation for the same model remains average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides a dense memory profile without the cost of additional unneeded CPU cores. This makes the server suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling, such as small-to-medium database operations, caching layers like Redis, and single-threaded data processing tasks.
